hypothesis: Descent-driven relaxation of the negative tail can recover useful tree updates when strict-tail proposals fail, with fewer futile loss evaluations from a tie-aware directional check.
budget_policy: Each proposed tree counts, including rejected proposals. Accepted tree counts, objective-call cost and wall time can differ.
reference_policy: Prior selected native baseline hyperparameters with tree cap 40; prefixes reselected on original validation. Additional earlier hyperparameter search is not matched.
scope: Fit/score training and original validation only. Source discovery reads later partitions for schema and source verification but no later prediction is computed. All four sources are consumed development sources.
primary_measure: Mean validation recall at empirical FPR budgets .0005 and .001, followed by lower mean FPR and higher AP.
claims_to_disprove: Adaptive continuation beats fixed-tail and clock schedule controls under the common proposal budget.
Checked and blind adaptive training have matching accepted trajectories and prefixes while checked uses fewer objective calls.
BAF stalling can be recovered by this proposed-tree-driven continuation.
falsifiers: If schedules match or beat adaptation, withdraw adaptive quality claim.
If checked differs in trajectory, investigate before attributing cost benefit to safe rejection.
If wall time rises despite fewer objective calls, report overhead rather than speedup.
descent_scope: Actual accepted working objective only. Fixed target loss may rise when relaxed. Exact nonnegative directional derivative excludes descent along that tree only; floating-point signs are not formal interval certificates.
prior_art: pAUC/DRO, continuation, curriculum, hard-negative mining and directional calculus are established. The specific tested scheduling and rejection mechanism is a novelty candidate, not an established first.
holdout_policy: No new calibration or final scoring. Previous final results remain unchanged.
withdrawn: V7 coupled prior/tree update did not exceed best static controls on any of the four sources; do not promote that mechanism.
